about: Step 5b: a spot-check of step 4's extractions, made by the Claude Code session that built this folder (not by a human scholar). For each version it read the 274e and 275a sentences of the stored passage against the Greek and asked: is each pharmakon rendering the word that stands for φάρμακον, and are the other slots filed under the right Greek word? Every pharmakon slot was checked in all seventeen versions; the other slots were checked where noted. A scholar should repeat this before citing anything.

checks.en-1892-jowett: Pharmakon slots correct: 'a specific both for the memory and for the wit' (274e), 'The specific which you have discovered is an aid not to memory, but to reminiscence' (275a). Note that at 275a Jowett uses two words for one pharmakon, 'specific' and 'an aid'; the 'not … but' contrast attaches to 'aid'. Jowett also replaces wisdom with truth at 275a ('not truth, but only the semblance of truth'): the extraction is right to file that under σοφίας δόξαν.
checks.en-1914-fowler: Pharmakon slots correct: 'an elixir of memory and wisdom' (274e), 'an elixir not of memory, but of reminding' (275a). Other slots correct.
checks.de-1804-schleiermacher: Pharmakon slots correct: 'als ein Mittel für den Verstand und das Gedächtnis' (274e), 'Nicht also für das Gedächtnis, sondern nur für die Erinnerung hast du ein Mittel erfunden' (275a). Schleiermacher reverses Plato's order (Verstand before Gedächtnis) and renders σοφία as Verstand, understanding. 'dünkelweise geworden statt weise' for δοξόσοφοι is correct.
checks.de-1853-georgii: Pharmakon slots correct (Hilfsmittel twice). Checked the reversal the model reports: Georgii does put Erinnern where Plato has μνήμη and Gedächtnis where Plato has ὑπόμνησις ('Nicht also für das Erinnern, sondern für das Gedächtnis hast du ein Hilfsmittel erfunden'), the opposite of Schleiermacher. The text is from a 1940 reprint; whether 1853 reads the same is unchecked.
checks.fr-1831-cousin: Pharmakon slots correct: 'C'est un remède que j'ai trouvé contre la difficulté d'apprendre et de savoir' (274e), 'Tu n'as donc point trouvé un moyen pour la mémoire, mais pour la simple réminiscence' (275a). One slot is misfiled: the extracted μνήμης (274e) 'mémoire' comes from 'soulagera leur mémoire', which renders μνημονικωτέρους. In the pharmakon clause Cousin turns 'of memory and wisdom' into 'against the difficulty of learning and knowing', so the 274e μνήμης is better read as 'apprendre' (or as not translated).
checks.fr-1922-meunier: Pharmakon slots correct: 'un remède pour soulager la science et la mémoire' (274e), 'Tu as trouvé le moyen, non point d'enrichir la mémoire, mais de conserver les souvenirs qu'elle a' (275a). Meunier's 275a makes writing a way of keeping memories, not of being reminded: a substantive reinterpretation the slot captures.
checks.it-1869-dalbono: Pharmakon slots correct: 'questo aiuto per la scienza e per la memoria' (274e), 'un mezzo di ritenere, ma di richiamare a memoria le cose' (275a). Filing 'ritenere' (to retain) under μνήμης at 275a is right.
checks.es-1871-azcarate: Pharmakon slots correct: 'un remedio contra la dificultad de aprender y retener' (274e), 'un medio de cultivar la memoria' (275a). The 274e μνήμης/σοφίας slots ('retener'/'aprender') are a judgment call: Azcárate, like Cousin, turns the genitives into 'the difficulty of learning and retaining', and which verb answers to which Greek noun is not determinable. The remède→moyen / remedio→medio pattern matches Cousin, which supports the inventory note that Azcárate may have worked from the French.
checks.ru-1863-karpov: Pharmakon slots correct: 'я изобрел ее, как средство для памяти и мудрости' (274e), 'ты изобрел средство не для памятования, а для напоминания' (275a). The σοφίας δόξαν slot is the one step 5 failed: the words are in the passage, but split by a footnote marker ('приобретут[175] у тебя') and quoted by the model without it. The guardrail was right to flag it; the reading itself ('мудрость … не истинную, а кажущуюся') is correct.
checks.pl-1918-witwicki: Pharmakon slots correct: 'lekarstwem na pamięć i mądrość' (274e), 'to nie jest lekarstwo na pamięć, tylko środek na przypominanie sobie' (275a). Witwicki changes word inside Thamus's sentence: memory gets a medicine (lekarstwo) that writing is not, reminding gets a mere means (środek). Step 5 counts this as 'same word for both', which is true of the slot but hides the switch.
checks.fi-1920-lehmuskoski: Pharmakon slots correct, and the model is right that they are two different compounds: 'apukeinoksi' (274e) and 'apuneuvoa' (275a), both built on apu-, help. 'rikkiviisauden' / 'rikkiviisaiksi' for σοφίας δόξαν and δοξόσοφοι checked.
checks.el-nd-gounaris: Pharmakon slots correct: 'της μνήμης και της σοφίας το φάρμακον' (274e), 'δεν εύρες φάρμακον μνήμης, αλλ' υπομνήσεως' (275a). The translation keeps Plato's words for pharmakon, mnēmē and hypomnēsis; it changes δοξόσοφοι to the ordinary δοκησίσοφοι.
checks.la-1484-ficino: Pharmakon slots correct: 'memoriae namque et sapientiae remedium id est inventum' (274e), 'non memoriae, sed commemorationis, remedium invenisti' (275a). Ficino keeps one word and Plato's genitives, so the turn survives intact. The σοφίας δόξαν slot ('opinionem potius, quam veritatem') leaves out 'sapientiae', which precedes it ('sapientiae quoque opinionem'): a fair extraction of the contrast, but read the full phrase.
checks.en-1792-taylor: Pharmakon slots correct: 'this invention is the medicine of memory and wiſdom' (274e), 'you have not diſcovered the medicine of memory, but of admonition' (275a). The stored passage includes Taylor's long footnotes, which the OCR runs into the text; the renderings come from the dialogue, not the notes.
checks.en-1848-cary: Pharmakon slots correct: 'invented as a medicine for memory and wisdom' and 'not discovered a medicine for memory, but for recollection'.
checks.en-1848-wright: Pharmakon slots correct: 'a medicine which I have discovered, both for memory and wisdom' and 'a medicine not for memory, but for recollection'. Text is the 1900 reprint.
checks.en-1871-jowett: Pharmakon slots right, but two neighbours are misfiled. Jowett 1871 reads 'this is the cure of forgetfulness and of folly' (274e; the OCR has 'forgetfulne^'): he inverts the genitives, so the remedy is against forgetfulness and folly rather than of memory and wisdom. The μνήμης (274e) slot should be 'forgetfulness' (inverted), not 'better memories' (which renders μνημονικωτέρους); the σοφίας (274e) slot 'folly' is right but inverted. At 275a he already has 'a specific, not for memory but for reminiscence', the word he carried back into 274e in 1892.
